question: Shab-e-Barat is referred to as the "Night of"
solution:
The correct answer is __**Atonement**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Shab-e-Barat** is a significant night observed by the **Muslim community**, primarily occurring on the **15th night** of the **Islamic month** of **Sha'ban**, which is the **eighth month** of the **lunar calendar**.
 
• The term is derived from the **Persian** word "**Shab**" meaning **night** and the **Arabic** word "**Bara'at**" meaning **immunity**, **deliverance**, or **forgiveness**. In the context of English terminology used in socio-religious studies, it is widely referred to as the **Night of Atonement** or the **Night of Records**. ***Hence, the option Atonement is correct.***
 
• It is believed that on this night, **Allah** (the Almighty) determines the **destiny** and **fortune** of all individuals for the **coming year**, including their **births**, **deaths**, and **provisions**.
